governance.templateInstructions: This repository uses the TCTBP workflow as a repo-specific profile. Preserve Time in Motion commands, docs paths, version source, tag format, status-report tables, deployment expectations, and local runtime conventions when updating these files.

simple.description: Single production branch only. Suitable for template repos, libraries, and non-deployed projects.

project.name: ddre-tim
project.description: Time in Motion monorepo with a Fastify API, shared contracts, and planned desktop and web clients.

profile.releaseBuildPolicy: No separate release build exists yet. Use `npm run build` as the normal build gate. Deploy remains disabled until a repo-specific runtime target exists.

maxFileLines.comment: AI agents and contributors should respect these file-size limits. Files at or above hardSplit must be split before checkpoint. Files above warningThreshold require a justification comment at the top.

modularity.comment: Prefer many small single-purpose files over large multi-purpose files. Extract a group of 3+ related functions into a dedicated module. Consider splitting a module when importing more than 8 symbols from it.

functionRules.comment: Keep functions small and focused. Prefer pure functions. Avoid 'any' in exported TypeScript signatures.

ship.purpose: Create a formal milestone ship from a clean, fetched branch, allowing first-time publication from a clean unpublished branch while keeping version, tag, and remote state recoverable and unambiguous. Use checkpoint, publish, or handover between routine slices instead of treating ship as the default sync action.

publish.purpose: Safely publish the current clean branch to origin, including first publication when no upstream exists yet, without bumping version, creating tags, or updating handover metadata.

checkpoint.purpose: Create a durable local-only checkpoint commit on the current branch so work is preserved without version, tag, metadata, or remote side effects.

shipReport.comment: At the start of SHIP, render a concise release-focused local-versus-origin snapshot table before making changes. Use 'n/a' where a row has no meaningful origin-side value.

statusReport.comment: For status, the first user-visible output block must be the fuller local-versus-origin comparison table using exactly the configured columns `Origin`, `Local`, `Status`, and `Action(s)`. Emit it as a standalone Markdown table block with a blank line before and after the table. Do not replace the table with prose, do not place prose on the same line as the table header, and do not emit a status-only reply without the table. Include the current branch, default branch, tags, ahead/behind state, and handover relevance. Use 'n/a' where no meaningful origin-side value exists.

handoverReport.comment: At the end of handover, render a concise five-row summary table that confirms the current branch, tag state, metadata branch publication, metadata consistency, and clean synced baseline. Emit it as a standalone Markdown table block with a blank line before and after the table. Keep it shorter than status and focused on the handover result.

checkpointReport.comment: At the end of checkpoint, render a concise summary table focused on the actual commit transition and the resulting local-only baseline. Emit it as a standalone Markdown table block with a blank line before and after the table. Include the previous HEAD commit, the new checkpoint commit, the resulting working-tree state, the branch sync state, and an explicit confirmation that remote state did not change. Use 'n/a' where no meaningful origin-side value exists.

branch.purpose: Safely close out the current published branch, reconcile the default branch, and either stop on the default branch or create the next work branch without losing code.

handover.purpose: Safely checkpoint and publish the current work branch at end of day, then refresh the handover metadata branch so another machine can resume from a deterministic shared state.
handover.checkpointPurpose: Preserve unpublished dirty work before verification or reconciliation can block handover, using a clearly marked non-release checkpoint commit or other repo-approved durable checkpoint.

resume.purpose: Restore the intended work branch at start of day by consulting handover metadata first, preserving current local unpublished work when a safe branch switch would otherwise strand it, and reconciling only through non-destructive checkout and fast-forward operations.

abort.purpose: Detect partial workflow states and recover safely without discarding unpublished work or rewriting history implicitly.

rules.resume: Suggest when the current machine is not yet on the intended handed-over work branch, the metadata points at a different published branch than the current branch, or the safest next action is to restore the last handed-over branch after preserving local unpublished work when needed.
rules.checkpoint: Suggest when the working tree is dirty and the safest immediate step is to preserve local progress with a local-only non-release commit before continuing or before deciding whether to publish or hand over.
rules.publish: Suggest when the current branch is clean, ahead of origin or missing an upstream, and the user likely wants to publish the branch safely without creating release version or handover metadata side effects.
rules.handover: Suggest when the active work branch must be left in a durable shared state for another machine or another session, especially when branch publication and handover metadata should be refreshed together before stopping work.
rules.ship: Suggest when there are unshipped commits since the last tag or version and tag drift exists.
rules.abort: Suggest when a partial workflow state is detected.
rules.none: Suggest when branch state is clean, synced, and no SHIP or handover is needed.

docsInfraPolicy.comment: For docs-only or infrastructure-only changes: skip heavy verification commands, keep editor diagnostics and docs impact assessment.

documentation.comment: Also review any architecture, workflow, or platform document directly affected by the change. Update the concrete docs list when desktop or web workspaces become implemented release surfaces.

deploy.failureMessage: Deploy is not configured for this repository yet. Define a repo-specific build, target, rollback plan, and post-deploy validation before enabling deploy.
deploy.purpose: Deploy is intentionally disabled for this repository until a repo-specific runtime build, publication, or installer distribution workflow is defined.

adviserContract.compatibility: Readers reject unsupported major versions, ignore unknown additive fields, and degrade by missing capability.

candidateGuard.comment: Promotion and release workflows should bind candidates to both commit and tree identities and revalidate them at approval boundaries.

promotionSafety.comment: Use read-only merge preflight and deletion impact checks before a mutating promotion merge.

releaseState.comment: Release journals are generic workflow evidence. Project-specific backup and restore stages must be added by downstream profiles rather than assumed by TCTBP-Web.

runtimeTransaction.comment: Runtime publication is an injectable atomic bundle transaction. Service lifecycle and health verification belong to the consuming project.

mergeDeletionAudit.stopMessage: This merge deletes {files} files ({lines} lines). Type 'confirm deletions' to proceed.
mergeDeletionAudit.hardStopMessage: This looks like a destructive tree reset, not a normal merge. Review carefully before proceeding.

prePushNetDeletionCheck.message: This push has a net deletion of {net} lines ({added} added, {removed} removed). Confirm this is intentional.

codeLossPrevention.comment: Code-loss prevention gates apply to branch closeout merges, promote merges, and any agent-performed merge into a default or environment branch.
